description: La toilette de la gitane signé et daté 'G. Doré/ 1868' (en bas à droite) pierre noire, plume et encre brune, lavis brun et rehauts du blanc sur papier signed and dated 'G. provenance: M. Paul Touzet Collection (according to the exhibition catalogue 1932) | Sale, Tajan, Paris, 25 March 2002, lot 237 | Private Collection, France | | Literature | H. Leblanc, Catalogue de l'oeuvre complet de Gustave Doré : illustrations, peintures, dessins, sculptures, eaux-fortes, lithographies : avec un portrait et 29 illustrations documentaires, 1931, p. 342, no 122. | | Exhibited | Palais des Beaux-Arts de la ville de Paris (Petit Palais), Gustave Doré 1832-1883, 1932, p. 21, no 94 | | | This intimate and sensitively rendered drawing was likely executed during Gustave Doré's journey to Spain in 1861, undertaken in the company of his friend and writer Jean-Charles Davillier. The two travelled extensively through the country, documenting their observations in what would become L'Espagne (see L'Espagne par le Baron Ch. Davillier, illustrée de 309 gravures dessinées sur bois par Gustave Doré, Paris, 1874, p. 133), a richly illustrated travelogue that combined Doré's incisive drawings with Davillier's descriptive text. | | The present drawing reflects Doré's fascination with the everyday life and customs of Spain, particularly among its Romani communities. Unlike the more theatrical or romanticised depictions often favoured by Orientalist painters of the period, Doré's drawing stands out for its naturalism and quiet dignity. The subject, absorbed in a private act of self-care, is portrayed with subtle empathy, free from caricature or sentimentality. | | Doré's Spanish journey marked a significant moment in his career, offering a counterpoint to his more monumental illustrative work and allowing him to explore a direct, observational mode of draftsmanship. This sheet is a compelling example of that personal engagement, imbued with the immediacy of travel and the artist's keen eye for human presence.

description: Oreste et Pylade investis par les bergers porte une inscription 'NORBLIN de la Gourdaine J.P. né 15/7/1745 mort 25/2/82/ ORESTE/ LAPIDE par les bergers' (au verso, sur le chassis) huile sur toile bears inscription 'NORBLIN de la Gourdaine J.P. né 15/7/1745 mort 25/2/82/ ORESTE/ LAPIDE par les bergers' (on the stretcher, on the reverse) oil on canvas 113 x 146.5cm (44 1/2 x 57 11/16in).
provenance: Private Collection, France | | Literature | P. Grunchec, Les Concours des Prix de Rome 1797-1863, Paris, Ecole nationale supérieure des Beaux-Arts, 1986, 2 vol., p. 77 | | Son of the renowned artist Jean-Pierre Norblin de La Gourdaine (1745-1830), Sébastien-Louis-Wilhelm Norblin de la Gourdaine (called "Sobeck"), continued the family's artistic tradition, focusing primarily on historical and genre scenes. | A pupil of M. Regnault he participate at the Prix de Rome competition in 1822 where he was first successful to the initial judging with the Death of Tullus Hostilius and then participated to the last judging with the present painting. | The preparatory of this painting, formerly attributed to Auguste-Hyacinthe Debay or de Bay (1804-18865), is conserved to the Ecole National des Beaux Arts, Paris (inv. PC 18081-1822-1, see P. Grunchec, Les Concours des Prix de Rome 1797-1863, Paris, Ecole nationale supérieure des Beaux-Arts, 1986, 2 vol., p. 78, pl. 4) | | His style shows the influence of both neoclassicism and early romanticism, reflecting the transitional aesthetic currents of his time. Though specific paintings from the Salon 1822 exhibition are not extensively documented, his participation highlights his engagement with the official art world of post-Napoleonic France.

title: Le rêve brisé
description: Le rêve brisé signé et daté 'GOTTARDUS WERNER- OSTROGOTHUS/ PX-MDCCCLXXIII.' (en bas à droite) huile sur toile signed and dated 'GOTTARDUS WERNER- OSTROGOTHUS/ PX-MDCCCLXXIII.' (lower right) oil on canvas 53.7 x 73.8cm (21 1/8 x 29 1/16in).
provenance: Private Collection, France | | Born in Linköping, Sweden, in 1837, Adolf Gotthard Werner studied at the Royal Swedish Academy of Fine Arts in Stockholm from 1857 to 1861, receiving the Meyerska Medal in 1859. He continued his artistic training in Antwerp and Paris under Émile Signol (1804-1892), and later at the Düsseldorf Academy, known for its academic rigor and emphasis on narrative painting. After extensive travels through France, Spain, and Italy, Werner settled permanently in Rome in 1869, where he became part of the expatriate artist community. | | Werner's work is marked by precise draftsmanship, detailed settings, and a strong sense of narrative, often rooted in mythological, allegorical, or moral subjects. Le Rêve brisé is a representative example of his mature style, depicting a young shepherd resting beside a broken vase, with mythological figures such as Cupid, Sappho, Euterpe, and Bacchus evoking themes of love, loss, and artistic inspiration. The composition combines classical references with a restrained emotional tone, reflecting the influence of both the Düsseldorf tradition and the Northern European artistic milieu active in Rome during the late 19th century. | | Werner exhibited in Sweden, Germany, and Italy, and his works are held in several public collections, including the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm and the Östergötland Museum.

title: La consolation

provenance: Private Collection, France |  | A pupil of Jean-Léon Gérôme (1824-1904), Hippolyte-Dominique Berteaux was known for his genre scenes, portraits, and decorative commissions. He exhibited regularly at the Paris Salon from 1866 and received several honours during his career. The present painting is a typical example of his work, marked by precise drawing, clear composition, and careful attention to costume and setting, in line with the academic tradition of the period. |  | Works by Berteaux are held in several French public collections, including the Musée d'Orsay in Paris and the Musée Antoine Lécuyer in Saint-Quentin.

provenance: Sale, Hôtel de Ventes de Monte-Carlo, Monaco, 30 April 2016, lot 35 | | Victor Gabriel Gilbert is renowned for his depictions of Parisian market scenes, a genre that became a hallmark of his career, gaining prominence in the 1880s. | | In the present painting, the artist captures the vibrancy of urban commerce, portraying market vendors and bourgeois figures with realism and social nuance. Exhibited regularly at the Salon and honoured with the Légion d'Honneur, Gilbert's work stands as a sophisticated commentary on the social and cultural rhythms of Paris during the Belle Époque. | | Another version of the present painting was offered at Christie's New York, 26 January 2011, lot 212. | | We are grateful to Noé Willer and Emilie Charmetant for confirming the attribution to Victor Gilbert. description: Portrait de la Princesse Doria huile sur toile oil on canvas 99.2 x 81.4cm (39 1/16 x 32 1/16in).
provenance: With gallery Elleni, 2000 where acquired by the present owner | Private Collection, Italy |  | This refined portrait by Eliseo Sala exemplifies the artist's mature style, distinguished by psychological subtlety and technical finesse. Trained at the Accademia di Brera and later influenced by the Roman and Venetian schools, Sala became one of the leading portraitists of mid-19th century Italy, favoured by the Lombard and Savoyard aristocracy. |  | Depicted with poised dignity, Princess Doria—likely a scion of the illustrious Genoese family—is rendered with a calm introspection that transcends mere representation. The restrained palette and precise handling of light and fabric reflect Sala's characteristic balance between academic discipline and quiet romanticism. |  | Typical of Sala's portraiture, the work is as much a study in noble identity as it is a testament to the cultural values of the Risorgimento era.

Throughout his career, Rossi balanced portraiture with genre scenes, achieving success in both Italy and France, where he regularly exhibited at the Paris Salon. His portraits, such as this refined example, demonstrate his sensitivity to character and atmosphere, hallmarks of an artist who moved fluidly between realism and a softer impression.

description: Vue du lac au coucher du soleil signé, daté et inscrit (partiellement illisible) 'Arthur Parton 1880/Boston' (en bas à gauche) huile sur toile signed, dated and indistinctly inscribed 'Arthur Parton 1880/Boston' (lower left) oil on canvas 96.7 x 71.5cm (38 1/16 x 28 1/8in).
provenance: Private Collection, France |  | A key figure associated with the second generation of the Hudson River School, Arthur Parton later embraced the more atmospheric sensibilities of American Tonalism. Trained at the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts and influenced by his travels in Europe, Parton developed a refined approach to landscape that prioritized mood and light over topographical detail. In the present work, the artist captures the subtle effects of dusk with a restrained palette and luminous handling of reflection and sky, characteristic of his mature work. The composition exemplifies his interest in conveying a contemplative vision of nature, bridging the romanticism of mid-19th-century American landscape painting with the tonal aesthetics that would dominate the turn of the century.

title: Vue du Bosphore
description: Vue du Bosphore signé 'Fabius Brest' (en bas à droite) huile sur toile signed 'Fabius Brest' (lower right) oil on canvas 35.2 x 60.2cm (13 7/8 x 23 11/16in).
provenance: Private Collection, France | Sale Claude Aguttes, Paris, 25 October 2013, lot 68, where purchased by the present owner | Private Collection, France |  | Pupil of Léon Cogniet, Germain Fabius Brest was renamed for his detailed landscapes and scenes of the Ottoman Empire, particularly Constantinople. His depictions of the Bosphorus, like much of his work, reveal his meticulous observation of natural and architectural forms, rooted in the traditions of French academic painting. Today, his work remains valued for its documentation of the East, its precise technique, and its historical significance within the Orientalist movement. His frequent travels to the Middle East in the mid-19th century fuelled his passion for Orientalist themes, a genre popular in European art at the time.

title: Un marchand de rue à Constantine
description: Un marchand de rue à Constantine signé et daté 'C Brun 1906' (en bas à droite) huile sur toile signed and dated 'C Brun 1906' (lower right) oil on canvas 59.5 x 38.5cm (23 7/16 x 15 3/16in).
provenance: Private Collection, France |  | A student at the École des Beaux-Arts in Paris under François-Édouard Picot (1786–1868) and Alexandre Cabanel (1823–1889), Guillaume-Charles Brun debuted at the Paris Salon in 1851. He became known for his genre scenes and Orientalist works, particularly those depicting everyday life in North Africa, such as in Algeria and the city of Constantine, as seen in the present painting. For a similar composition, see Christie's, New York, 25 October 2006, lot 56.
